title: The Art of the Dewclaw: Purpose and Care
description: Explore the often-overlooked dewclaw, its evolutionary purpose, and essential care tips for your feline or canine companion.
main_content: Dewclaws are the digits located higher up on a paw, analogous to a thumb in humans. In many species, they serve as a gripping aid when climbing or holding prey. For dogs, dewclaws on the front paws are functional, providing traction when running and turning. Rear dewclaws, common in breeds like the Great Pyrenees, offer extra stability on rough terrain. In cats, dewclaws are highly functional for climbing and grasping. Care involves regular trimming to prevent overgrowth, checking for injuries, and cleaning the nail pocket to avoid infection. Some dogs have double dewclaws, a trait prized in certain breeds. Always consult a vet before considering removal, as dewclaws have important functions.
key_takeaways: Dewclaws serve as a thumb-like digit aiding grip and stability.
Front dewclaws are functional in most dogs; rear dewclaws vary by breed.
Regular maintenance includes trimming and checking for debris or injury.
Removal should only be considered for medical reasons, not cosmetic.
